objective: Standard statement: (1) a long edge with k capped pairs acts by 9^k (P+ + t P-), t = (-1/3)^k, so the count of a system whose L negated incidences are replaced by long edges is 9^(kL) times a polynomial of degree at most L in t, whose value at t = -1 is the signed count and at t = 1 the count with the signs dropped; (2) long edges and their caps inside planar pieces keep SOFT-CROSS A's Pfaffian certificate; (3) switching inside the pages leaves the soft crossing with 6 negations; (4) Theorem: counting proper 2-colourings of 3-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs whose incidence graphs are Pfaffian is #P-hard under Turing reductions (composition with SOFT-CROSS B, Theorem 4); (5) demonstration: 9 #col(K3,3) recovered from plain Pfaffian instances only (k_S = 1, 3, 5, 7, with L = 6 k_S long edges and L + 1 lengths each), plain instances certified at small lengths, signed host edges handled the same way. Controls: t = 1 gives the plain count; L counts leave the value at t = -1 undetermined. Nearest known result: Fan-Cai 2020 (hard on general graphs, planar case in FP); on Pfaffian graphs none found.
status: Proved: counting 2-colourings of 3-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs with Pfaffian incidence graphs is #P-hard (Turing); a long edge read at t = -1 is a negation, certificates survive, and 9 #col(K3,3) = 54 is recovered from 100 plain Pfaffian counts (largest 18504 vertices).
title: Signs interpolate away: plain Pfaffian triple systems are #P-hard to count
